comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `untrackedFailingChecks` can never carry a name through `computePrStatus` — the "names ride the status" contract this PR documents is unreachable in the wiring it ships**

The module header (this line, plus the smProvider status doc at `smProvider.js:27-31`) and the PR description promise the *status* carries the failing names: *"the status and the factory-state cards carry `untrackedFailingChecks`/`untrackedFailing` (names + failed-run links)"*. Through the status path the census is provably always `[]`:

- The reconcile fires only when the tracked fold reads `green`/`none` (`isReconcilableVerdict`).
- The fold (`_ghCheckOutcome`/`_ghTallyRollup`) reddens on ANY `FAILURE`/`TIMED_OUT` entry of the same rollup the census walks — so whenever the reconcile fires, the census over that same rollup finds nothing: a visible failure would have made the fold `red` (no reconcile), bokeping failures are folded out of both, a commit-status (`state`-spelling) failure pendings the fold (`!c.conclusion` → `'pending'`), and a nameless failure reddens the fold while the census skips it.
- Verified exhaustively against the real helpers for every rollup shape (visible failure, `timed_out`, bokeping-only, cancelled+green, status-context `FAILURE`, older-failure-under-newer-success, empty): every firing case carries `untrackedFailingChecks: []`. The PR's own live-shape test pins this (`test_mergeStateReconcile.js:391` — "census empty (invisible to the check-runs API)"), and the `reason` string therefore always ends in the `(not in the check-runs rollup)` fallback.

Consequences:

1. **Misleading telemetry on exactly the path this PR exists to make diagnosable.** The next freeze will show `untrackedFailingChecks: []`, which reads as "nothing failing found" when it means "invisible from this vantage". The reason string disambiguates, but the field name, the AC1/AC3 docstring here (`mergeStateReconcile.js:14-15`), the smProvider header (`smProvider.js:27-31`) and the PR description all advertise names on the status.
2. The per-tick census in `_ghReconcileCheckVerdict` (`failingCheckNames` over every rollup: bokeping folding + latest-per-context sorting) is dead computation on the status path — the name-bearing audit actually lives on the factoryState card path (`untrackedFailing`, which has the runs list).
3. The AC1 unit test (`test_mergeStateReconcile.js:290`) pins the naming capability with an input the wiring can never produce (`checkConclusion: 'green'` alongside a `failure` IN the rollup) — green-box coverage of an unreachable path.

Suggested fix (docs-only is acceptable): amend the contract so the status registers the **fact** (raw `mergeStateStatus` + empty census + reason) while the failing **names** ride the factory-state cards — i.e. reword `mergeStateReconcile.js:14-15`, the smProvider status doc, and the PR description. Optionally drop the census from the status wiring (don't pass `rollup`) so the payload shape cannot promise names it cannot carry — or rename the field on this path so `[]` can't be misread as "no untracked failure".

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: an unlatched GUEST PR with an untracked failing check now has no reacting lane at all — the same freeze shape gh-140 closes, one lane over**

Post-PR (this switch to `trackedChecks`, and its twin on `review-threads-resolved`), the effective verdict of an untracked-failure head reads `red`. That is the intended trigger for the machine's bounded red-head flow — but that flow is machine-author-only, and switching the re-review armers off the effective verdict leaves the guest lane on it while nothing else covers guests:

- `review-external-once` (the guest one-time review, `checks: "green"`, `notMachine: true`) no longer arms: an untracked red reddens the effective verdict.
- `fail-validation` needs the `ai_validating` latch; `rework-on-red-gate-unlatched` is explicitly machine-author-only ("auto-rework is machine-only, owner rule"); `review-machine-unlinked` is `prMachineAuthor: true`.

So for an external PR whose head carries a failing untracked check while unlabeled (e.g. the repo's own `docs-freshness` workflow failing on any head — exactly the gh-1392 red), pre-PR the fold read green and the review armed; post-PR nothing arms: no review, no rework, no park until someone latches it. The PR strands silently until the red clears by luck — the "no lane reacts" freeze this very PR was opened to close (gh-140/gh-1392), reintroduced for guests.

Suggested fix: gate `review-external-once` on `trackedChecks: "green"` as well (one line). Its dedup survives the switch — while its review leg runs, the leg's own check run pendings the fold, and `trackedVerdict` (the pre-reconcile fold) reads `pending`, so the rule stays excluded; with an untracked red it would arm the review on a head that still cannot merge (mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE keeps `merge-validated-guest` gated), which matches the PR's own economics: "an untracked red must freeze the rework flow, not the re-review economy". If deliberately keeping guests frozen is the owner's call, say so in the PR description.

Related doc gap worth one sentence either way: the other effective-verdict readers (`review-machine-unlinked`, `review-after-dev`, `develop-done` `prChecks`) also now pause on untracked reds until the red-head rework resolves — for `review-machine-unlinked` that ordering is load-bearing (its structural dedup is expressed through the effective fold), so documenting "non-review lanes deliberately stay on the effective verdict" stops a future green-gate cleanup from "fixing" it into a freeze or a duplicate-review bug.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGESTION: the BLOCKED exclusion leaves the required-check variant of the same blind spot open**

`mergeStateReconcile.js:32-34` excludes BLOCKED with the rationale *"with a green fold a BLOCKED report is the conversation-resolution gate (gh-828), not a check failure"*. That holds for the gh-828 conversation case, but GitHub also reports BLOCKED when a **required** check is failing/pending — and if that required check sits outside the tracked set (commit-status spelling, or a repo workflow the rollup does not surface), the freeze this PR closes recurs in a different spelling:

- fold reads `green`/`none` → reconcile skipped (BLOCKED not in `UNSTABLE_MERGE_STATES`);
- the effective verdict stays green → `merge-validated` (`checks: "green"`) fires → the merge attempt hits GitHub's BLOCKED refusal → no `fail-validation` lane (the fold never reddened) → the head strands exactly like gh-1392, with no rework lap.

If a BLOCKED + green-fold head with no unresolved conversation is reachable in the deployments this runs on, extending the reconcile (or arming rework off the merge-refusal path) would close the variant; otherwise one line in the module doc naming the residual ("BLOCKED with a green fold is assumed to be the gh-828 conversation gate; a required untracked check would strand") prevents the next archaeology session. Deliberate per the docstring — flagging the incomplete rationale, not asking to flip the decision in this PR.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGESTION: the census's provenance pointer is wrong, and the newest-wins walk now exists in two places**

`mergeStateReconcile.js:84` says *"Same key order as smProvider.latestCheckRunConclusions"* — no such symbol exists on smProvider; the function lives at `js/smAgent.js:8048` (`latestCheckRunConclusions` + its `isBookkeepingCheckName` companion, which deliberately imports the canonical prefix list "so the two verdict readers cannot drift"). With this PR the latest-per-context walk (completed_at → started_at → id → position, bookkeeping folded out) exists in:

1. `js/smAgent.js:8048` — `latestCheckRunConclusions` / `eachNonBookkeepingConclusion`
2. this module — `latestConclusions` / `failingCheckNames` (the superset: camelCase stamps + `databaseId`)

The module is require-free by design (smProvider/factoryState require it — the reverse would cycle), so the clean unification keeps purity AND kills the drift surface: the census already lives in this pure module, so `smAgent.js` could require it instead of owning its own copy (its requires are hoisted top-level, so the gh-823 deferred-require pin stays happy; this module requires nothing back). The new superset semantics (camelCase stamps, `databaseId`) would then back both readers, and the prefix list would come from one place. If that is follow-up-sized for this PR, at least fix the pointer to `js/smAgent.js:8048` so the next reader does not hunt for a symbol that is not there.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGESTION: `_ghRawMergeStateStatus` re-implements `normalizeMergeStateStatus`**

`smProvider.js:541-543` hand-rolls the exact chain the new module exports one call away — `mergeStateReconcile.normalizeMergeStateStatus(pr.mergeStateStatus || pr.mergeable_state || null)` (trim → uppercase → empty→null, null/undefined-guarded). This file already requires the module (hoisted per gh-823, cycle-free), so the local copy is a drift surface without an isolation benefit: a future hardening tweak to the shared normalizer (say, rejecting non-string garbage explicitly) would silently skip this call site. Reusing the export keeps the "never a fabricated verdict" contract defined in exactly one place.

comments.body:
🪶 severity: NIT —
🪶 **NIT: the tracked fold is computed twice per prStatus**

`computePrStatus` evaluates `_ghCheckConclusionLabel(rollup, tally)` once inside `_ghReconcileCheckVerdict` (feeding the reconcile) and again at `smProvider.js:445` in `_ghBuildPrStatus` for `trackedVerdict`. The results are definitionally identical (same pure inputs) — computing it once and threading the label through (or reusing `rec.trackedVerdict` when the reconcile fired) would make that equality structural instead of incidental. Nothing behavioral; readability/economy only.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-140 reconcile works end-to-end (tracked-green fold + reported UNSTABLE/FAILED → effective red → the bounded red-head flow reacts; AC2 payload stability holds; full unit suite passes locally: 9054/9054). Two important issues: the status-path audit overclaims (`untrackedFailingChecks` is provably always `[]` via `computePrStatus` — names only materialize on the factory-state cards), and an unlatched guest PR with an untracked red now has no reacting lane at all (review-external-once gated; guests have no rework lane).

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `untrackedFailingChecks` can never carry a name via the status path — misleading telemetry + dead per-tick census + an unreachable AC1 fixture (`js/common/mergeStateReconcile.js:14`)
- ⚠️ Unlatched guest PR with an untracked red: `review-external-once` gated, no guest rework lane → silent strand, the gh-1392 shape one lane over (`sm_github.json:697`)

- 💡 `_ghRawMergeStateStatus` duplicates `normalizeMergeStateStatus` (`js/common/smProvider.js:541`)
- 🪶 `_ghCheckConclusionLabel` computed twice per prStatus (`js/common/smProvider.js:445`)

**Next Steps**:
1. Align the AC3 contract with reality: status registers the fact (raw state + reason), names ride the cards — reword the module/PR-description claims, drop or reshape the dead status census
2. Switch `review-external-once` to `trackedChecks: "green"` (or document the deliberate guest freeze) and note the effective-verdict reader split in the PR description
3. Reuse `normalizeMergeStateStatus`, compute the fold once; consider routing smAgent's census through the pure module
